articles.title: Women's college basketball top storylines: JuJu's return, familiar names and transfer mania
articles.summary: Here 's what you need to know before the season tips off.
articles.body:
Women's college basketball begins anew Sunday when the 2026-27 NCAA Division I season opens at the Palazzo dello Sport in Rome. The Eternal City Tip-Off will feature No. 13 Notre Dame, with Player of the Year contender Hannah Hidalgo, and Villanova, a Big East foil to mighty Connecticut.

It's an appetizer to a full day of hoops on Monday , featuring the long-awaited return of 2025 Naismith and Wooden National Player of the Year JuJu Watkins. The dynamic 6-foot-2 USC guard redshirted the 2025-26 season to rehab the ACL injury she sustained in the 2025 NCAA tournament. She looked up to speed participating in Team USA's National Team training camp during Final Four weekend in April and expects to "peak at the right time" as the season progresses.

The return of Watkins is the top storyline of the season with UCLA as the defending champion and UConn's Sarah Strong holding Player of the Year honors. The NCAA tournament expanded to 76 teams (32 automatic bids, 44 at-large) and the Final Four is scheduled for April 1-4 in Columbus. Here are more things to know before tip-off.

USC's season opener against UNLV in the Hall of Fame Series at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas on Monday (4 p.m. ET, CBS Sports Network) will be 589 days since Watkins' injury. It's a longer timeline than other elite players who have come back. Former Texas point guard Rori Harmon returned to play 10 months after her injury , and POY Paige Bueckers from UConn returned at around the one-year mark.

Watkins led USC to back-to-back Elite Eights as one of the most talented scorers in the country (25.5 career ppg). As a sophomore, she nearly carried the Trojans as the main scoring catalyst before the injury in the second round . She'll have more help with reigning National Freshman of the Year Jazzy Davidson (No. 1 recruit in 2025) and freshman wing Saniyah Hall, also a No. 1 recruit.

The Trojans will be a top contender in the deep Big Ten (a record nine teams in the AP Top 25) and for the national title. USC won back-to-back championships in 1983 and 1984 but hasn't been back to the final since 1986.

It could be the final collegiate season for Watkins, whose pro-ready game as a freshman drew conversation around draft-eligibility rules. Watkins is age-eligible for the draft, but could also choose to come back to USC for a final year. She'll be in early NPOY contention alongside Strong, Texas' Madison Booker, Hidalgo and Vanderbilt's Mikayla Blakes.

South Carolina, UConn remain cream of crop

Is it even November if we're not talking about the embarrassment of riches on the campuses in Storrs, Connecticut, and Columbia, South Carolina?

After a fiery Final Four meeting that ended with a scuffle between UConn head coach Geno Auriemma and South Carolina's Dawn Staley, the powerhouses are built to meet again on the final weekend. It is the third consecutive season they have been ranked 1-2 in the AP preseason poll, with South Carolina earning the top spot this year. The last Final Four without either team was in 2007.

The 2026 runner-up Gamecocks won big in the offseason when five-star forward and ESPN No. 3 recruit Oliviyah Edwards requested a release from her national letter of intent to Tennessee, which underwent a massive roster overhaul . The 6-foot-3 dunking star opted for South Carolina, where she'll be a foundational frontcourt piece alongside All-Americans Joyce Edwards and Chloe Kitts. Kitts said she is 100% after missing the 2025-26 season with an ACL injury. Staley also added junior guard Jordan Lee, an unexpected transfer loss for Texas.

Its non-conference schedule is as loaded as ever. South Carolina will play No. 20 Maryland (Monday), No. 12 North Carolina (Nov. 8), No. 3 USC (Nov. 15), No. 2 UConn (Nov. 24) and No. 4 Duke (Dec. 3) within the first month of the season. The SEC schedule will offer plenty more résumé boosters.

Strong is fresh off sweeping National Player of the Year awards, and UConn added a freshman class that includes No. 2 recruit center Olivia Vukoša and Serbian guard Jovana Popovic.

Auriemma also scheduled quality squads to counteract the less-loaded Big East schedule. UConn will play No. 5 Michigan (Nov. 5), No. 10 Iowa, No. 18 Ohio State, No. 7 Louisville, No. 1 South Carolina, No. 4 Duke, No. 20 Maryland, No. 13 Notre Dame, Tennessee and No. 9 LSU.

Complete roster overhauls are becoming standard fare. UCLA chipped away over the early years of the bustling transfer portal to build the 2026 national championship squad , understanding that the top six in their rotation were all seniors. Head coach Cori Close was forced to reload all at once by adding senior forward Addy Brown (Iowa State), Elina Aarnisalo (UNC), Donovyn Hunter (TCU) and Bonnie Deas (Arkansas).

Iowa State lost all but three players on its roster, including senior Audi Crooks (Oklahoma State) and Jada Williams (LSU). The Cyclones have 10 new players — seven international players — in Bill Fennelly's final season as head coach. He's the Big 12 leader in wins and 15th overall in career victories (822).

Nine players departed Oklahoma State, though head coach Jacie Hoyt answered by adding Associated Press second-team All-American Crooks. The 6-foot-3 senior averaged 25.8 points per game, second in NCAA Division I, as an efficient interior presence (61.1% shooting from the floor). The Cowgirls also added Liv McGill, a 5-9 junior point guard who averaged 22.5 points, 6.1 rebounds and 6.3 assists per game a year ago for Florida. The program has not made it out of the second round since 2014.

Tennessee drew outsized attention for its postseason departures following a late-season collapse in Kim Caldwell's second season. The storied Lady Vols went winless in March for the first time in program history and not a single player returned. Caldwell added two freshmen and 13 transfers, headlined by All-Big Ten first-team guard Kaylene Smikle from Maryland and forward Aaliyah Moore from Texas.

Parity overall is growing on the women's side, but the top is still dominated by familiar characters. UConn and South Carolina combined for eight of the last 13 titles. UCLA (2026), LSU (2023), Texas A&M (2011) and Maryland (2006) are the only first-time winners over the past two decades.

The Final Four teams repeated in 2025 and 2026. While that isn't likely to be the case again — UCLA is completely transformed and Texas lost key pieces around Booker — the top teams are still a familiar group. Will there be a rare new champion this season?

No. 4 Duke, the two-time ACC tournament champion, has yet to win a title after falling in the 1999 and 2006 championship games. Head coach Kara Lawson is fresh off winning ACC Coach of the Year and the FIBA World Cup gold medal with Team USA. She returns All-ACC forward Toby Fournier and added standout sophomore guard Aaliyah Crump from Texas.

No. 5 Michigan has never made it into the Final Four, but could this season behind an elite junior class of top three scorers Olivia Olson, Syla Swords and Mila Holloway (though Holloway is sidelined indefinitely with a foot injury). They combined for 45.8 of the team's 82.3 points per game last season. All five of their top scorers return, and they'll add Stanford transfer Courtney Ogden.

No. 8 Vanderbilt bowed out of the NCAA tournament early, entering the 2026-27 season with a hunger built off missed opportunity. The Commodores last reached the Elite Eight in 2002, the last of their four regional semifinal runs. They return one of the best duos in Division I. Blakes is the reigning Ann Meyers Drysdale Award winner as the top shooting guard in DI and a finalist for Naismith Player of the Year, while sophomore Aubrey Galvan quickly emerged as one of the best playmakers in the country.

images.caption: Coach Dawn Staley of the South Carolina Gamecocks and coach Geno Auriemma of the UConn Huskies exchange words during the fourth quarter of the Final Four at Mortgage Matchup Center on April 3, 2026, in Phoenix. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) (Christian Petersen via Getty Images)

articles.title: El Río Breogán se pasea en el derbi gallego
articles.standfirst: Brown (22), Alonso (19), Bolton (16) y Andric (16) comandan la paliza lucense
articles.summary: Brown (22), Alonso (19), Bolton (16) y Andric (16) comandan la paliza lucense
articles.body: El Río Breogán, con un notable acierto exterior y su habitual juego coral en ataque, liquidó el derbi gallego frente al Obradoiro en el arranque del tercer cuarto, cuando golpeó a su rival con un escandaloso parcial 6-23 que Diego Epifanio no logró cortar con un tiempo muerto. El partido parecía sentenciado (49-73), pero el equipo santiagués apretó en defensa y desde ahí empezó a soñar con la remontada. Se acercó a 13 (60-73, min.27), que no fueron 11 por un error arbitral. Entonces, la apuesta de Luis Casimiro por jugar con dos bases acabó resolviendo el duelo. Bajo la dirección del croata Dominik Mavra, decisivo con sus asistencias, Breogán recuperó la renta de 20 puntos (62-82) con tres triples consecutivos, uno de Tevin Brown y dos de Rasir Bolton. El derbi arrancó con mucho acierto en ambos lados de la pista. Obradoiro castigaba la defensa rival con su acierto desde la línea de tres puntos -4 triples seguidos-, pero le faltaba intensidad para cerrar su aro. Además, Breogán anotaba con facilidad, con Josep Peris desatado. El intercambio de golpes era continuo (24-27, 34-33), pero la sensación era que Breogán estaba mucho más cómodo. Obradoiro aceptó jugar al baloncesto de ida y vueltas, y ahí el equipo de Casimiro es imparable. Con un parcial 0-8 en el último minuto y medio del segundo asalto, se marchó al intermedio con una renta de siete puntos (43-50). Aunque el veterano entrenador no lo quiera decir, este Breogán es un serio candidato a jugar la Copa del Rey. Mavra es el director de una orquesta donde Brown, Francis Alonso y Rasir Bolton castigan desde el perímetro, donde Andric asume con brillantez su rol secundario (14 puntos y 22 créditos de valoración) y donde Brankovic lo hace bajo el aro. 90.- Monbus Obradoiro (22+21+19+28): Childress (7), Barcello (18), Leo Meindl (11), Abogidi (-) y Joel Soriano (22) -cinco inicial-; Agada (11), Alejandro Galán (4), Sergi Quintela (4), Dos Anjos (2), Barrueta (11) y Alonso Faure (-). 110.- Río Breogán (20+30+32+28): Tevin Brown (22), Rasir Bolton (16), Peris (6), Andric (16) y Kasibabu (2) -cinco inicial- Mavra (11), Andersson García (6), Francis Alonso (19), Aranitovic (-), Brankovic (12) y Vicedo. Árbitros: Emilio Pérez Pizarro, Fabio Fernández y Guillermo Ríos. Incidencias: Encuentro correspondiente a la sexta jornada de la Liga Endesa disputado en el Multiusos Fontes do Sar ante unos 6.000 espectadores.

articles.title: Wemby Explains What the Brain Needs 'to Have Fun' After Scoring 43 and Getting 'WemVP' Chants
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama's brain is learning "pattern recognition" and what to do to "have fun" on the court as the San Antonio Spurs big man continues to dominate the NBA in his fourth season.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama's brain is learning "pattern recognition" and what to do to "have fun" on the court as the San Antonio Spurs big man continues to dominate the NBA in his fourth season.

"It's like pattern recognition," he told reporters after Saturday's 121-111 win over the Minnesota Timberwolves that included the crowd chanting "WemVP" (30-second mark). "The brain, after playing so many games, literally hundreds of games now in the NBA, knows what kind of game to go towards to have fun.

"Because whenever we don't score, it's like negative feedback. Whenever we score, we get good results, positive feedback for the brain. Over time, you recognize patterns, and you err towards those patterns. There's always ups and downs, but we're turning in the right direction."

Wembanyama earned that positive feedback with a career-high 34 shot attempts on his way to 43 points, seven rebounds, four assists, six blocks and one steal.

He showed off his entire arsenal of weapons with three-pointers on the outside, a number of dunks around the rim and incredible shot blocking on the defensive side. The Timberwolves, who were playing without their own star in Anthony Edwards, had no chance against him for much of the contest.

San Antonio has now won four in a row following a disappointing 0-2 start with losses to the Oklahoma City Thunder and Houston Rockets.

Wembanyama has been aggressive on the offensive end with 29 or more points in each of his last three games, including when he poured in 36 points in an overtime victory over the Utah Jazz.

While he is just six games into the young season, he is averaging what would be a career-high 28.0 points a night and looks like an MVP in the making.

The crowd certainly thought so as he dominated the Timberwolves on Saturday.

articles.title: Notre Dame stages late comeback to knock off Villanova in Rome to open men's college basketball season
articles.summary: The Irish trailed 66-60 with less than four minutes to go before winning 74-70.
articles.body:
Notre Dame overcame a six-point deficit in the final four minutes to beat Villanova 74-72 to officially begin the 2026-27 men's college basketball season.

The two Catholic universities met in the Eternal City Tip-Off in Rome in honor of Chicago-born and Villanova alum Pope Leo XIV. Villanova controlled most of the game, but the Irish scored five straight points to steal the win. Literally.

As Notre Dame trailed 68-67, Gonzaga transfer Braeden Smith got a steal with 1:29 to go. Smith slowed the pace down after pushing it into Villanova's half, and found a wide-open Logan Duncomb at the top of the key. The senior big man wasn't afraid to shoot, and buried the go-ahead jumper.

Smith's steal was Notre Dame's 14th of the day.

After Villanova missed a shot, Smith buried two more free throws to give the Fighting Irish a two-possession lead with 24 seconds to go.

Villanova had a chance to tie the game with under 10 seconds remaining, but Elijah Crawford's mid-range jumper didn't fall.

The pope was not in attendance on Sunday, but he did meet with the teams after they arrived in Rome.

Both Smith and Brady Koehler had 16 points for Notre Dame, while Villanova's Tyler Perkins had 18. Smith also had four steals as Villanova committed 20 turnovers. The steals allowed Notre Dame to win despite shooting 35% from the field.

articles.title: El Kosner Baskonia se desmelena en el primer triunfo de Perasovic
articles.standfirst: Simmons (22+1+5), Stewart (17+4+3) y Joksimovic (15+6+3) comandan el triunfo vitoriano ante el Kids&Us Manresa
articles.summary: Simmons (22+1+5), Stewart (17+4+3) y Joksimovic (15+6+3) comandan el triunfo vitoriano ante el Kids&Us Manresa
articles.body: El Kosner Baskonia de Velimir Perasovic consiguió este domingo su primer triunfo desde que el croata llegó a su banquillo y se impuso al Kids&Us Manresa por 106-83, en un duelo en el que salió a relucir la calidad individual de los azulgranas en la sexta jornada de la Liga Endesa. Kobi Simmons en la primera parte y DJ Stewart tras el descanso lideraron al equipo vitoriano, que se repuso a una desconexión tras el paso por vestuarios para sentenciar el partido antes del último asalto y dejar al Manresa sin victorias en la liga. El base cerró el choque con 27 créditos de valoración, mientras que por el lado visitante Yordan Minchev fue el más regular con 12 puntos y 14 rebotes. Los visitantes comenzaron más inspirados de cara al aro en un partido que empezó con bajas revoluciones. El tiro libre ayudó a los azulgranas a entrar en un partido en el que Notae y Joksimovic movían el árbol en uno y otro lado. Once puntos de Kobi Simmons con tres triples consecutivos dieron otro aire al partido y colocaron a los locales por delante con un importante parcial de 11-0, en un primer asalto con un inusual acierto exterior, 30-22. Las faltas personales y las pérdidas de balón fueron un lastre para lo de Diego Ocampo. Ongenda cometió su tercera falta en el arranque del segundo periodo y condicionó la rotación interior de un equipo que sufría defensivamente. El cuarto triple de Kobi Simmons mantenía la distancia baskonista sobre el Manresa, que mejoró en su disposición en las dos canastas y no se fue del partido. La energía defensiva del Manresa le permitió recortar distancias y frenar el ritmo anotador de un Baskonia que funcionaba mejor con velocidad. Un triple de AJ Lawson devolvió la calma en el marcador para el Baskonia al descanso, 50-40. Los de Ocampo entraron con mayor concentración tras el paso por vestuarios y estrecharon el cerco sobre un Baskonia que ganaba enteros con AJ Lawson y Kobi Simmons en pista. Yordan Minchev lideró la reacción del conjunto manresano, que le dio la vuelta al partido con un 6-18 en solo cuatro minutos. La calidad de los azulgranas, con DJ Stewart a la cabeza, recuperó el sitio para los locales, que volvieron a tomar el mando del partido con otro gran parcial, 24-4, que estuvo cerca de dejar sentenciado el duelo (83-64). La distancia se fue ampliando en un partido más roto y descontrolado que se le hizo demasiado largo a un Manresa que cosechó su sexta derrota en seis partidos. 106 - Kosner Baskonia (30+20+33+23): Simmons (22), Joksimovic (15), Lawson (16), Stewart (17) y Santos (5) -cinco inicial-, Frisch (10), Baugh (2), Spagnolo (10) y Faried (9). 83 - Kids&Us Manresa (22+18+24+19): Benítez (8), Notae (10), Tamba (2), Vila (2) y Ongenda (8) -cinco inicial-, Kolenda (11), Minchev (12), Beaufort (6), Bassas (3), Pumarola (3), Agbo (9) y Oriola (9). Árbitros: Rafael Serrano, Javier Torres y Javier Ávila. Sin eliminados. Señalaron falta flagrante a Notae (min. 4) y técnica al banquillo visitante (min. 26). Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la sexta jornada de la Liga Endesa disputado en el pabellón Fernando Buesa Arena de Vitoria ante 7.194 espectadores. Antes del partido se guardó un minuto de silencio en memoria de los fallecidos en el accidente ferroviario en Toledo.

articles.title: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander at loss for words after Chet Holmgren injury adds to Thunder’s brutal pile-on
articles.summary: The Oklahoma City Thunder have been hit as hard as any team in recent NBA history by the injury bug in the first week of the 2026 NBA season, recently losing...
articles.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder have been hit as hard as any team in recent NBA history by the injury bug in the first week of the 2026 NBA season, recently losing Chet Holmgren for the foreseeable future with a knee issue. Holmgren joins Cason Wallace and Jalen Williams as long-term injury absences for the Thunder, all of which were suffered in the same game last week vs the Los Angeles Clippers.

Now, Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has shared his candid reaction to the brutal injury luck at this early portion of the season.

"I don't know. We have some figuring out to do for sure," he said, when asked how the Thunder can adjust to their new reality, per Clemente Almanza of Thunder Wire on X, formerly Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

He also showed his support for Holmgren amid the tough setback.

"He loves the game. He works hard," he said.

The injuries to Holmgren and Williams in particular have caused some fans to wonder whether the Thunder might have to have some difficult conversations about potentially moving one or both of the former All-Stars, considering that both have been massive injury red flags throughout the course of their careers thus far.

One thing that no one in Oklahoma City wants to see is a year of SGA's prime being wasted, so it would not be a surprise to see general manager Sam Presti begin to work the phones and see if he can cash in on some of the Thunder's future assets in order to bring in a win-now player.

In any case, the Thunder have now lost two straight games in ugly fashion and will next hit the floor on Monday vs the Cleveland Cavaliers.

articles.title: Pac-12 men’s 2026-27 season preview
articles.summary: The first season of this iteration should be a lot of fun to watch
articles.body:
The Pac is back! The 2026-27 College Basketball season will mark the return of the Pac-12 after a two-year hiatus. However, after changing its name back in the early 2010's, the new version of the Pac-12 will only have nine teams. The league is filled with former Mountain West schools, two former Pac-12 schools, a WCC powerhouse and a former Sun Belt team. The combination is sure to provide exciting games and could be the best league in all of mid-major basketball.

Gonzaga will enter the new Pac-12 with the best roster in the conference. The Zags do have eligibility questions, but if Xaivian Lee and Javon Bennett remain eligible and if Chauncey Wiggins gets eligible, Mark Few could have one of the best teams in the sport. If they aren't eligible, Gonzaga is still the favorite in the Pac-12 by a decent margin.

Braden Huff is one of the best offensive players in the country whom Gonzaga greatly missed at the end of last season. Massamba Diop and now eligible Izan Almansa make a formidable duo defensively at the center spot. In the backcourt, we'll see what kind of stability they can get out of Nathan De Sousa, and I'm high on a Davis Fogle sophomore year breakout. Luca Foster and Isiah Harwell give Gonzaga some depth on the wings.

Once again, a Utah State head coach performed well and catapulted himself into a high-major job. With Jerrod Calhoun gone, the Aggies had to hire a new coach again. Ben Jacobson had been in Cedar Falls for two and a half decades and now he heads to Logan for a new adventure. Jacobson's success and experience in the Missouri Valley made him a more than viable candidate for the job, and he's got a nice roster for his first season there.

Utah State is another team with eligibility questions as for now, Dallin Hall and Connor Turnbull are good to go. That will be one of the better point guard/center duos in the league, but everything still goes as Mason Falslev goes. Falslev is entering his fourth season with the Aggies, and this will be his third different head coach. He's stuck it out and has won a lot of basketball games in Logan as a result. Elsewhere, Jacobson added two additional transfer guards in AJ Bates and Solomon Callaghan as well as bringing Will Hornseth with him from UNI. Hornseth and Karson Templin are both solid options at the four and is likely the position battle to watch for this group.

Brian Dutcher's team missed the tournament last year for the first time since 2019. As a result, there was a concerted effort to improve the offense after back-to-back seasons finishing outside of the top-90 nationally. That's going to start with Chance Gladden, an efficient point guard from Boston University. They're going to pair him with potential breakout candidate Elzie Harrington.

The frontcourt provides some question marks as Bear Cherry was excellent his first season at Sacramento State but missed most of last season with an injury. The Aztecs will also bring back Tae Simmons and Latrell Davis in addition to getting Isaiah Sy from Oregon State. This doesn't feel like an SDSU team that produces a top-20 defense, but the offense feels significantly better. I trust Dutcher to get the most out of his guys.

Oregon State moved on from Wayne Tinkle and made a big-time hire with Michigan assistant coach Justin Joyner. From the get-go, Joyner showed he wanted to add size in the frontcourt and athleticism/creation in the backcourt. The Beavers added two 7-footers in Xavion Staton and Dennis Evans. Not many teams at the mid-major level can say they have one 7-footer, let alone two.

The backcourt is maybe more impressive than the frontcourt. Josiah Lake II and Daniel Freitag could be one of the highest scoring backcourts at the mid-major level. I have been high on Freitag since he was in high school, and he really showed out at Buffalo last year. DeShawn Gory and Jackson Rasmussen give Joyner more proven scoring for a team that will have plenty. The team isn't super deep, but if Legend Smiley breaks out they have a real solid top seven.

Listen to the Pac-12 men's basketball preview podcast:

Listen to the Pac-12 women's basketball preview podcast:

The Ali Farokhmanesh era has hit year two, and the Rams will look to take a leap in a new league. They bring back Carey Booth, Jase Butler and Kyle Jorgensen. All were solid last year, but specifically with Booth and Butler, there could be more to their game.

Colorado State's second favorite team is apparently Marist as Justin Menard and Josh Pascarelli will both lead the backcourt with one of my favorite freshmen in the league: Pops Dunson. Dunson is a super quick guard out of Georgia who seems to get wherever he wants on the floor. He is probably their best backup point guard option with JoJo McIver out. We often see teams take major leaps in a coach's second season, and Colorado State could be no different.

Boise State has been a fairly consistent program in the Mountain West over the past five years and now in Pac-12, and I don't expect much to change. The Broncos started off the season poorly but bounced back to reach 20 wins for the sixth time in the last seven seasons. If they want to make it seven out of eight, keeping Lamar Washington eligible is imperative.

Boise State might have a short bench, but the starting five is strong. Damari Wheeler-Thomas had a great junior season at North Dakota State, and the Broncos will get Julian Bowie back from injury. Bowie had the makings of a breakout candidate before he missed most of last season. Leon Rice is replacing a lot in his frontcourt, and he will rely on a step up from Spencer Ahrens as well as Campbell transfer Dovydas Butka. The starting five should keep this team competitive with the top of the league.

It hasn't quite clicked for David Riley at Wazzu after a stellar tenure at Eastern Washington. We'll see if he can turn things around this year after a 12-win season last year. He'll need to hit on some transfers including Lazerek Houston, who was one of the best players at the Division-ll level last season. Elsewhere, you have to hope for breakouts from both Tyler Kropp and Jaylen Harrell, who are moving down from high-major schools.

If Wazzu gets a couple of breakouts and Houston is a big-time addition like many think he could be, this Washington State offense could be a thrilling watch. I have many questions about the defense though and a lack of a true rim protector. There's a chance that Kropp (only 2.6 block rate) is the only rotation player taller than 6-foot-8. That'll be a major hurdle when going up against the frontcourts that Gonzaga, Utah State, Colorado State and others have.

Texas State had some major upgrading to do after joining the Pac-12, and while it is evident that they are still a bit behind their peers, this team can certainly sneak up on some teams to get wins. Quel'Ron House was a good point guard in the Missouri Valley last year and will be the point guard for the Bobcats.

Despite the House addition, this team still runs through DJ Hall, who had an outstanding freshman season averaging over 15 points and seven rebounds per game. He was terrific for a team that closed the season red hot. The Bobcats will have to get contributions from their role players elsewhere if they want to compete with some of the better teams in this league, but this roster is a step in the right direction.

I have to give some credit to Vance Walberg here. In his first two seasons Fresno State finished higher than their preseason KenPom expectation. There's certainly a chance that Fresno State can do that again and still finish ninth in the league. After all, this league is really good and someone will have to finish last.

Dragos Lungu was an intriguing pick up from UT Martin and should be one of the featured guys offensively. The Bulldogs do have some size with Bradey Henige and Baye Fall, which will be important when they play some of the better teams in this conference. What has me concerned about Fresno State at this point is the inexperience in the backcourt. Neither KJ Perry nor Roger Fabrega Urpina has played a single minute of Division-l basketball, and that's going to certainly hurt you when you're going up against the experienced backcourts in this league on a nightly basis.

articles.title: Valkyries crowned WNBA Champs with Game 7 win over Dream
articles.summary: On Saturday, the Golden State Valkyries were crowned WNBA Champions after a thrilling win over the Atlanta Dream in Game 7.
articles.body:
Although the Golden State Warriors had the day off, Chase Center was still at the center of the sports world on Saturday afternoon. In only their second season in franchise history, the Golden State Valkyries hosted Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream in a winner-take-all Game 7 to decide the WNBA Championship.

While the Valkyries opened the game with an early lead throughout the first quarter, momentum swung in favor of the Dream in the second quarter. The Dream's lead grew to as many as nine points in the third quarter.

However, Gabby Williams wouldn't let the Dream close out the Valkyries in the Bay Area. The All-Star forward tallied 13 points in the fourth quarter to go along with fiery 28 points in the second half. Behind Williams, the Valkyries stormed back to take the lead and run away with a 68-63 win in Game 7.

In only their second season in the WNBA, the Valkyries were crowned WNBA champions for the first time in franchise history.

Williams notched 30 points on 10-of-23 shooting from the field with four made 3-pointers to go along with four blocks, three rebounds, two assists and two steals in 38 minutes on her way to winning WNBA Finals MVP.

Tiffany Hayes and Veronica Burton each scored in double-figures for the Valkyries. Burton registered a double-double with 10 points and 10 rebounds in Game 7 against the Dream.

Golden State rookie Yaxel Lendeborg was in attendance and got to meet Williams after the game.

The Valkyries' defense held Reese to eight points on 3-of-7 shooting from the field with a game-high four turnovers. Reese added 12 boards, two blocks and an assist in 33 minutes. Jordin Canada and Allisha Gray were the only members of the Dream to score in double figures.

Chase Center will have to clean up the confetti and re-open their doors on Sunday when the Warriors host the Los Angeles Clippers for contest at 5:30 p.m. in San Francisco.

articles.title: El Valencia Basket pasa el rodillo en Andorra
articles.standfirst: Saint-Supery (17+2+6 recuperaciones), Brooks (23 con 5/9 triples) y Sako (8+11) lideran el triunfo taronja ante el MoraBanc Andorra
articles.summary: Saint-Supery (17+2+6 recuperaciones), Brooks (23 con 5/9 triples) y Sako (8+11) lideran el triunfo taronja ante el MoraBanc Andorra
articles.body: El Valencia Valencia Basket pasó este domingo por encima del MoraBanc Andorra de Žan Tabak, que desapareció en los últimos 10 minutos, en los que encajó un parcial de 11-34, y sufrió una derrota escandalosa (79-111). La igualdad y las rotaciones en el banquillo fueron la nota predominante de los primeros 10 minutos. El MoraBanc Andorra aguantó el tipo después del 6-11 inicial de parcial del Valencia Basket y, con los puntos de Artem Pustoyvi y Kassius Robertson, reaccionó y ganó el primer cuarto por 21-20. En el segundo cuarto, el equipo de Xavi Albert despertó con un parcial de 1-11 para situar el 22-31 con dos mates seguidos de Nael Sako. Tabak pidió tiempo muerto y sus jugadores respondieron hasta el 34-37. A partir de entonces, el parcial del Valencia Basket fue de 3-13 para conseguir la máxima diferencia (+12, 34-46). Kassius Robertson, que jugaba contra uno de sus exequipos en la ACB, anotó cinco puntos seguidos, los últimos tres sobre la bocina con un triple para el 39-46. Tras el descanso, Armoni Brooks fue el gran protagonista del Valencia Basket. El escolta estadounidense, que había anotado 10 puntos hasta el intermedio, se fue hasta los 23 en el tercer cuarto con cuatro triples. Los de Tabak compitieron, pero no pudieron con la calidad ofensiva de los de Xavi Albert. Al final del tercer cuarto se llegó con un 68-77 y 31 puntos recibidos por el MoraBanc. Un parcial de 11-34 explica lo que pasó en el último cuarto. El MoraBanc desapareció de la pista de manera incomprensible y el Valencia Basket le paso por encima con un destacado de Mario Saint-Supéry, que anotó 12 puntos en los últimos diez minutos. 79 - MoraBanc Andorra (21+18+29+11): Akinjo (17), Best (5), Wes Iwundu (3), Cam McGriff (3) y Pustovyi (19) -cinco inicial-; Robertson (18), Mutic (2), Radošević (5), Kuric (6), Andronikashvili (-), Owen Aquino (1) y Chumi Ortega (-). 111 - Valencia Basket (20+26+31+34): TJ Shorts (8), Saint-Supéry (17), Taylor (11), Osetkowski (6) y Sako (8) -cinco inicial-; Álvaro Cárdenas (-), Brooks (23), Jasiel Rivero (7), Josep Puerto (13), Corbalán (8), Moore (8) y Lucas Marí (2). Árbitros: Alfonso Olivares, Sergio Manuel y David Sánchez. Eliminaron por cinco faltas a Cam McGriff (m.37), del -MoraBanc Andorra. Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la jornada 6 de la Liga Endesa en el Pavellón Toni Martí ante 2.898 espectadores.

articles.title: Brizuela aúpa al Barcelona y condena a sus ex del Unicaja
articles.standfirst: El escolta azulgrana decide con un triple a 37,2 segundos del final... y Perry falla dos para mandar el partido a la prórroga
articles.summary: El escolta azulgrana decide con un triple a 37,2 segundos del final... y Perry falla dos para mandar el partido a la prórroga
articles.body: El Barcelona consiguió su primera victoria del curso en ACB fuera de casa en el Carpena ganando a un buen Unicaja por 89-92. El partido, que por momentos fue malagueño, se decidió en un triple cuando el balón quemaba de Darío Brizuela en la penúltima jugada del partido. El Barça, obligado a remontar tras una primera mitad en la que estuvo claramente por debajo, encontró en Joel Parra a su principal referente y en Punter, Martin y Brizuela los jugadores capaces de decidir el choque cuando más apretaba el marcador. El duelo arrancó con el Unicaja imponiendo un ritmo altísimo. La circulación de balón, la intensidad defensiva y el acierto exterior permitieron a los locales tomar rápidamente el control del encuentro. Perry abrió el camino desde el perímetro y Hunt añadió energía y puntos para llevar el marcador hasta el 14-6. El Barcelona trataba de responder con Brizuela y Evbuomwan, pero los malagueños mantenían la iniciativa. La entrada de Willy Hernangómez añadió otro foco de atención al partido, aunque el protagonismo continuaba siendo local. Perry, especialmente inspirado, puso el broche al primer cuarto con una brillante acción desde la media distancia para cerrar los primeros diez minutos con 29-25. El segundo periodo mantuvo la misma tendencia. Kravish castigaba desde posiciones intermedias y Hunt encontraba espacios para lanzar desde fuera, mientras Noua se incorporaba también al festival de triples. El Unicaja llegó a abrir una brecha de doce puntos con el 42-30 y el Carpena disfrutaba de una de las mejores versiones de su equipo. El Barça necesitaba cambiar el rumbo y Punter asumió la responsabilidad con dos triples que devolvieron a los visitantes al partido. Aun así, los de Vidorreta no se dejaron arrastrar por la reacción azulgrana y consiguieron alcanzar el descanso con una ventaja de nueve puntos, 54-45, después de un triple de Perry y una penetración de Hunt. Tras el intermedio llegó la reacción del Barcelona. Parra apareció con fuerza y los visitantes recortaron rápidamente la diferencia, mientras Robinson y Martin ayudaban a completar la remontada. El Unicaja perdió parte del control que había tenido en la primera mitad y acabó viendo cómo Umude colocaba al Barça por delante. Los locales, sin embargo, no se descompusieron. Kalinoski devolvió el golpe desde el perímetro y Pantzar asumió cada vez más responsabilidad para mantener vivo al equipo. El tercer cuarto terminó con empate a 72 y el encuentro entró en sus diez minutos definitivos completamente abierto. El Barça logró ponerse cinco arriba, pero Pantzar respondió desde la línea de tiros libres y devolvió la ventaja al Unicaja con el 81-80. A partir de ahí, cada posesión tuvo valor de sentencia. Martin volvió a dar ventaja al Barcelona, pero Kravish apareció bajo el aro para poner nuevamente por delante al Unicaja a menos de un minuto del final. El Carpena empujaba, pero Brizuela silenció al pabellón con un triple que situó el 89-90. Perry tuvo entonces la oportunidad de cambiar la historia, pero su lanzamiento exterior no entró. Punter aprovechó la siguiente acción para ampliar la diferencia desde el tiro libre y dejó al Unicaja con 12,5 segundos para buscar el empate. La defensa azulgrana cerró todas las opciones y Perry tuvo que lanzar un triple complicado. El balón no quiso entrar y el Barcelona terminó llevándose un partido que durante muchos minutos había pertenecido al Unicaja. 89 - Unicaja (29+25+18+17): Perry (15), Hunt (16), Kalinoski (3), Noua (5), Kravish (15) -quinteto inicial-, Pantzar (12), Barreiro (6), Lukosius (6), Brazdeikis (0) y Hernangómez (11). 92 - Barça (25+20+27+20): Robinson (6), Martin (11), Umude (9), Parra (17), Nebo (5) -quinteto inicial-, Punter (13), Brizuela (10), Ubal (2), Nkamhoua (8), Evbuomwan (8) y Minaya (3). Árbitros: Antonio Conde, Arnau Padrós y Cristóbal Sánchez. Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la jornada 6 de la Liga Endesa disputado en el Palacio de los Deportes José María Martín Carpena, que registró un lleno con 10.681 espectadores. Se guardó un minuto de silencio en memoria de las víctimas del accidente ferroviario en Urda (Toledo).

articles.title: 2 Dream most to blame for WNBA Finals loss to Valkyries
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream came within one victory of winning their first-ever WNBA championship but ultimately fell short against the Golden State Valkyries, losing...
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream came within one victory of winning their first-ever WNBA championship but ultimately fell short against the Golden State Valkyries, losing 68-63 in Game 7 in the WNBA Finals . Gabby Williams eventually took charge of a low-scoring affair where both teams struggled to find consistent offensive production.

Atlanta went in at halftime leading by six points , and had actually gone ahead by as many as nine in the third quarter before eventually allowing the Valkyries to take over the game. Jordin Canada and Allisha Gray carried much of the scoring responsibility, combining for 34 points, but Rhyne Howard and Angel Reese struggled to provide enough offense, while the supporting cast offered limited help.

We look at the Atlanta players most to blame for the WNBA Finals loss to Golden State, who won their first title in just the second year of their existence.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

#1 Rhyne Howard left Atlanta without a third option

Howard's offensive struggles were among the biggest problems for Atlanta in Game 7. She finished with just six points, six rebounds, three assists and three steals, failing to provide the scoring support the Dream needed alongside Canada and Gray.

While she was a constant menace on defence, the Dream were left starved of scoring and needed the four-time All-Star to step up. Howard ended the season averaging 17.7 points per game per Basketball Reference, but was unable to make the same impact when her team needed it the most.

Howard's six points ultimately left Atlanta short of another reliable scoring threat during decisive stretches, which put further pressure on the likes of Canada and Gray.

#2 Angel Reese needed to get more points

Reese finished with eight points, 12 rebounds, one assist, one steal and two blocks, shooting 3-of-7 from the field. Her rebounding remained valuable, but she struggled to convert consistently against Golden State's interior defense and did not make a single field goal in the fourth quarter.

With Howard, Atlanta's second option behind Gray enduring a difficult night, it was Reese who could have been the answer for her team. Reese's struggles in Game 7 concluded a four-game run that saw her contribute just 38 points, a stark contrast to the 65 points she scored in the first three games of the series. The Valkyries undoubtedly double-teamed Reese and made things uncomfortable in the paint as much as they could, but Reese will be well aware that things could have gone starkly differently.

The defeat marked another missed opportunity for Atlanta, who lost the WNBA Finals for the fourth time since 2010. Game 7 was an extremely low-scoring affair, and there is no doubt a few extra points from the above-mentioned stars could have helped Atlanta script history.

However, as Reese herself claimed, this might only be the start of the journey for this group of players, and there is no doubt that the Dream have the talent to make another serious run at the title in the coming years.

articles.title: Luka Doncic gets an early message from Bam Adebayo ahead of Lakers-Heat showdown
articles.summary: Bam Adebayo has a plan for slowing Luka Doncic, and he shared it before the Miami Heat headed to Los Angeles.
articles.body: Bam Adebayo has a plan for slowing Luka Doncic, and he shared it before the Miami Heat headed to Los Angeles. The Heat face the Lakers on Monday night at Crypto.com Arena, the first stop on a five-game West Coast trip.Doncic is averaging 36.2 points in his first five games, which gives Miami plenty to solve. The Slovenian star also scored 37 in the Lakers’ 112-95 loss at Golden State on Oct. 30. The Heat opened 0-4 but have won two straight, and Adebayo kept his message short and simple.What did Bam Adebayo say about guarding Luka Doncic?Bam Adebayo told reporters on Sunday how Miami will handle Luka Doncic, and the plan is not complicated. “We’re just going to try and make him make difficult shots,” he said. Miami wants Doncic to see two defenders and think before acting, and the goal is to get other Lakers to miss. Adebayo added other teams around the league do the same thing.Miami has the personnel to try it. Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo anchor the Heat defense, and Doncic is also averaging 7.6 assists and 6.8 rebounds, so sending help is not a clean fix. The Lakers were 4-2 before Sunday’s game against Toronto. A win in Los Angeles would give Miami a boost after its 0-4 start and extend its two-game streak.Can the Lakers hold up when Doncic sits?Miami may not need a perfect plan if Los Angeles keeps giving ground when Doncic rests. The Lakers have been outscored 164-119 in the 60 minutes and 41 seconds Doncic has sat across five appearances. The figure leaves out the Oct. 28 game against the Clippers, which Doncic missed with back tightness. The Lakers won it 103-87, and Collin Sexton scored 21.The Warriors game showed the gap. Los Angeles was plus-9 during Doncic’s 37 minutes and 21 seconds and minus-26 over the other 10:39. Golden State’s bench outscored the Lakers’ reserves 50-7, and Sexton went 0-for-6. Austin Reaves had eight turnovers, six of them with Doncic on the floor, and the team gave it away 22 times in all.Coach JJ Redick was direct afterward. “Got to figure the turnover thing out,” he told reporters.With Doncic on the floor, the Lakers have a 130.7 offensive rating and a plus-17.9 net rating. Adebayo’s plan fits that split. Make the star work, then see if the supporting cast can make Miami pay.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Steve Kerr Praises Gabby Williams, Valkyries After 2026 WNBA Finals Win vs. Angel Reese, Dream
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr greatly enjoyed watching the Valkyries win Saturday's Game 7 WNBA Finals matchup against the Atlanta Dream, 68-63, winning a title in just their second year of existence.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr greatly enjoyed watching the Valkyries win Saturday's Game 7 WNBA Finals matchup against the Atlanta Dream, 68-63, winning a title in just their second year of existence.

"Awesome. Just an incredible game," he told reporters. "The drama, the grit. Just a typical Game 7. Finding a way. Gabby Williams just erupting in that second half was amazing to watch. ... As a basketball fan I think you embrace games like that. Just watching what it takes, the competitive desire of both teams and everything on the line. And how fun it is for us as fans and how incredibly stressful it is for the teams involved."

The aforementioned Williams was the hero, posting 28 of her 30 points in the second half.

It was a historic moment for the Valkyries, and Kerr was among many in the Bay Area who enjoyed watching it all transpire.

articles.title: NBA suspends Hawks rookie Kingston Flemings for 'intentionally elbowing' Pelicans' Bryce McGowens in the head
articles.summary: Flemings will miss Monday's game against the Indiana Pacers without pay.
articles.body:
The NBA suspended rookie Atlanta Hawks guard Kingston Flemings one game for "intentionally elbowing" New Orleans Pelicans guard Bryce McGowens in the head, the league announced Sunday.

The incident took place during the Pelicans' 121-99 win over the Hawks on Saturday. Flemings will miss Monday's game against the Indiana Pacers without pay.

The incident took place late in Saturday's game as the Pelicans held a big lead.

Flemings elbowed McGowens twice in same sequence

Flemings delivered a forearm to McGowens' face in a clearout as he drove to the basket in transition. McGowens blocked the shot despite getting hit in the face, and the two landed near each other on the baseline.

This isn't what got Flemings suspended. As the two ran back up court side-by-side, Flemings delivered an elbow to Flemings head that in no way resembled a basketball play.

A scuffle ensued in the aftermath of the contact. Officials reviewed the play and issued Flemings a technical foul and ejected him from the game. The Pelicans held a 119-93 lead in the game's final minutes when Flemings delivered the elbow.

Flemings, 19, has played seven NBA games. The Hawks selected him with the No. 8 overall pick in June's NBA Draft after his standout freshman season at Houston.

In 20.1 minutes per game, Flemings is averaging 7.1 points, 4.6 assists, 2.9 rebounds and 0.9 steals while shooting 47.6% from the floor and 38.5% from 3.

articles.title: Wemby Reveals Gregg Popovich's Most Important Lesson Before Stepping Down as Spurs HC
articles.summary: San Antonio Spurs superstar Victor Wembanyama appeared on 60 Minutes Sunday night and passed along an important lesson he learned from legendary former head coach Gregg Popovich.
articles.body:
San Antonio Spurs superstar Victor Wembanyama appeared on 60 Minutes Sunday night and passed along an important lesson he learned from legendary former head coach Gregg Popovich.

"He often said something when we were in film: 'After a win, you're rarely as good as you thought you were, and after a loss you're rarely as bad as you thought you were,'" Wembanyama said.

Wemby, 22, came into the 2026-27 season among the frontrunners to win the MVP this season and has looked the part thus far, averaging 28 points, 10.7 rebounds, three assists, 1.3 steals and an absurd 4.2 blocks across six contests.

Perhaps more importantly, however, he's trying to get the Spurs back to the NBA Finals after the team fell short against the New York Knicks last season. Navigating that challenge, and his own continued efforts to improve, provides plenty of challenges. But Wemby seems to relish wading into the unknown.

"I think the key is being comfortable not knowing, being comfortable finding out my own answers," he told 60 Minutes , "I am comfortable not knowing my answers. I am comfortable walking through the fog."

articles.title: Hawks' Kingston Flemings Suspended By NBA for Intentionally Elbowing Pelicans Player in Head
articles.summary: The NBA announced Sunday night that Atlanta Hawks guard Kingston Flemings has been suspended for a game after elbowing Bryce McGowens in the head during the fourth quarter of Saturday's 121-99 loss against the New Orleans Pelicans.
articles.body:
The NBA announced Sunday night that Atlanta Hawks guard Kingston Flemings has been suspended for a game after elbowing Bryce McGowens in the head during the fourth quarter of Saturday's 121-99 loss against the New Orleans Pelicans.

Flemings intentionally popped McGowens in the face away from the play and was ejected.

Flemings, 19, has appeared in seven games thus far for the Hawks during his rookie season, averaging 7.1 points, 4.7 assists and 2.9 rebounds per game while shooting 47.6 percent from the field and 38.5 percent from three.

The No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NBA draft has shown some flashes early in his career, including a 23-point game against the Miami Heat on Oct. 28.

His dirty elbow from Saturday night was a bad look, however, and led to a scrum on the court.

He'll miss Monday's game against the Indiana Pacers due to his suspension. The Hawks (3-4), who have lost four of their last five games, will be looking to move back to .500 against the Pacers.

articles.title: Wemby Talks NBA Finals 'Villain' Label, Blood Clot Diagnosis and More in New '60 Minutes' Interview
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama was only in his third year in the league when he led the San Antonio Spurs to the NBA Finals last season, but that didn't stop him from being labeled as the villain in the series against the New York Knicks.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama was only in his third year in the league when he led the San Antonio Spurs to the NBA Finals last season, but that didn't stop him from being labeled as the villain in the series against the New York Knicks.

Reflecting on that label, Wembanyama said he didn't give it any attention at the time.

"No, it didn't because I'm not paying attention to this when you're in the Finals," he said on 60 Minutes . "I don't think any player on either team really is."

Wembanyama said playing in the Finals also helped him learn more about himself as a player.

"It showed my limits more than anything else," he said. "Going out there, you need to play basketball; you don't need to beat the s--t out of people."

His blood clot diagnosis in 2025 helped him reflect on things off the court.

Wembanyama's passion and intensity are second to none, and that perhaps sometimes comes out in ways that lead to him earning a villain label. Whether he'll continue to embrace it remains to be seen.

But while Wembanyama might be the villain in the eyes of other teams, he said his favorite play is one that requires great connection with his teammates.

"I think alley-oops in particular," he said. "Alley-oop is a team play and also a dunk. I like alley-oops."

Wembanyama is a rare player for many reasons, but the biggest is his combination of size and skill. The league has never seen someone at his height who can handle the ball and shoot like a guard.

It also means he doesn't have a player he can look to as the model for how to succeed.

"I am comfortable not knowing my answers. I am comfortable walking through the fog," Wembanyama said.

While he can't turn to former players as mentors the way some players can, he's managed to find inspiration in other ways, like a trip to China last offseason.

Wembanyama, who became the league's first unanimous Defensive Player of the Year last season, is off to a great start this year, putting up 28.0 points, 10.7 rebounds, 4.2 blocks and 1.3 steals per game.

articles.title: Atlanta Hawks rookie faces suspension after controversial elbow to opponent sparks disciplinary action
articles.summary: The NBA has suspended Atlanta Hawks rookie Kingston Flemings for one game without pay.
articles.body: The NBA has suspended Atlanta Hawks rookie Kingston Flemings for one game without pay. The league says the guard intentionally elbowed New Orleans Pelicans guard Bryce McGowens in the head during Saturday’s 121-99 loss. It happened with 3:04 left in the fourth quarter. Officials gave Flemings a technical foul and ejected the rookie, and a short scuffle followed in which New Orleans’ Julian Reese also drew a technical. Flemings will miss Monday’s road game against the Indiana Pacers, a night when the Hawks already have four players listed as questionable or out.What did Kingston Flemings do to earn a suspension?The league ruled the contact was deliberate and said the elbow landed on McGowens’ head. The 19-year-old threw it while running back up the floor, and the whistle came fast. A review ended with the ejection.Flemings had 12 points, six assists and two rebounds in 25 minutes off the bench before the ejection. The No. 8 pick in the 2026 draft out of Houston is averaging 7.1 points, 4.7 assists and 2.9 rebounds this season. The suspension costs the guard one game check, and Flemings is due back Wednesday against the Washington Wizards.How will the Hawks cover for Flemings against Indiana?Flemings is the only true point guard on the roster, so the gap is hard to fill. The rookie was coming off the best game of his young career, with 23 points, five assists and five rebounds against Miami last Wednesday. The injury report came out Monday, and the suspension followed shortly after, which left Atlanta little time to adjust.Aaron Wiggins is expected to take heavier minutes. Two-way guard RayJ Dennis could get first regular-season action. Dennis has played well in the G League for Atlanta, but NBA minutes are a different test.The frontcourt is the bigger problem. Jock Landale, Mouhamed Gueye and Henri Veesaar are out, and Jalen Johnson is questionable. If Johnson sits, second-year forward Asa Newell should get a larger role. Newell played over 18 minutes Saturday after Landale went down early, finishing with 13 points and four rebounds. Shooting was a struggle, and defense is still a work in progress.Even with Johnson available, Newell likely plays. Rookie Zuby Ejiofor could log first minutes of the season. He took third-center minutes in the preseason but saw little court time, and the question mark is shooting. Dorian Finney-Smith, who has played small-ball center before, is a wildcard.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Luka Dominates for Lakers vs. Raptors, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Reaves, Kessler, Top Players
articles.summary: Luka Dončić has been cooking to start the 2026-27 season. The Toronto Raptors were just the latest team to get barbecued.
articles.body:
Luka Dončić has been cooking to start the 2026-27 season. The Toronto Raptors were just the latest team to get barbecued.

The Los Angeles Lakers' superstar put up a 45-point, 15-rebound double-double in his team's 131-125 win over the Raptors on Sunday night.

Here's a look at the game's top performers:

Dončić was plus-27 on the night, an absurd number. He has truly entered, "You can't stop him, you can only hope to contain him" territory early this season.

Perhaps his only blemish on the night was his seven turnovers. The Lakers in general were a bit loose with the ball, coughing it up 22 times. But it was an otherwise perfect performance from Dončić.

And it was a nice return to form for the Lakers' offense in general. L.A. scored at least 125 points in each of the first four games of the season before averaging 99 points in the two games coming into Sunday night. The Lakers were particularly effective from deep, shooting 18-of-37 (49 percent) from three in the win.

JJ Redick likely won't be thrilled that the Lakers took their foot off the gas in the fourth quarter, getting outscored by the Raptors 43-27 and turning a potential blowout into something a bit too close for comfort. But the Lakers held them off, moving to 5-2 on the season.

They'll next host the Miami Heat on Monday night. The 3-3 Raptors are also in action on Monday night and are staying in Los Angeles to face the Clippers.

articles.title: Lakers’ Luka Doncic is not having it with Scottie Barnes’s shenanigans during Raptors game
articles.summary: Luka Doncic wasted little time asserting his dominance against the Toronto Raptors in Sunday’s game for the Los Angeles Lakers. By halftime, Doncic appeared...
articles.body:
Luka Doncic wasted little time asserting his dominance against the Toronto Raptors in Sunday's game for the Los Angeles Lakers . By halftime, Doncic appeared fully focused on securing the victory and showed little interest in entertaining Scottie Barnes' antics.

During the game, Barnes and Doncic got tangled up with each other during a play, leading to a tense exchange between the two. Barnes appeared to be trying to provoke the Slovenian star into reacting and potentially drawing a foul, particularly with Luka already dealing with foul trouble. However, Doncic refused to take the bait.

Ultimately, though, it was Doncic who had the last laugh as the Lakers bounced back from their disappointing loss to the Golden State Warriors with a 131-125 win over Toronto.

Against Scottie Barnes and the Toronto Raptors, Luka Doncic delivered one of the most remarkable individual performances against the franchise in recent memory.

The Slovenian superstar finished with 45 points, 15 rebounds, six assists, five steals, and one block. He was also highly efficient offensively, converting 12 of his 23 field-goal attempts, knocking down eight of 12 shots from beyond the arc, and making all 13 of his free throws.

According to Stathead, Doncic became the only player in NBA history to record such a stat line in a single game. The performance also marked the 71st 40-point game of his career, including the postseason.

Doncic's dominance was evident from the opening quarter, as he wasted little time taking control of the game. He poured in 16 points in the first 12 minutes, marking the fourth time this season he has scored at least 15 points in the opening quarter. Remarkably, the rest of the NBA has combined for only four such performances during the same span.

Having surrendered a significant advantage in its previous matchup against the Golden State Warriors, the Lakers desperately needed a convincing response, and Sunday's performance provided exactly that. The win also improved Los Angeles' record to 5-2 on the season.

articles.title: Victor Wembanyama speaks on how his blood clot problem in 2025 changed his life
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama has spoken about the blood clots he got that led to him learning a big lesson.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama has proven that he is one of the league's best players over the past three years. However, he has already dealt with some serious health problems, but they were not the lower-body injuries that people thought he would get in the NBA.

The biggest health scare that Wembanyama has faced was the blood clots he dealt with in early 2025. It was such a big part of Wemby's life that he made sure to learn a lot of lessons from that scary experience that prematurely ended his 2024-25 campaign with the San Antonio Spurs .

Victor Wembanyama reveals the lessons he learned from his blood clot issues

Wembanyama has always dealt with problems head-on, which is why he is such a good player. However, the deep vein thrombosis or blood clots were a problem that he struggled against, especially since, if it was worse, it was life-threatening. Thankfully, Wembanyama listened to the medical professionals, so that led to him having a much better life.

It has also changed his outlook on his personal life and career. That is a big deal for Wembanyama because it felt like he grew up during that debacle with the blood clots. That helped him mature and be more expressive, which is why that was a big part of the Spurs ' run to the NBA Finals last season.

Now, Wembanyama is a much more emotional person because he knows that he does not have to hide anything after going through what he went through. Wemby is much more vocal with his team, and his team understands that he is more expressive now.

"The condition I had in early 2025, the thrombosis, had a huge impact on this. After that it's like, life's so short, I don't even want to waste it being somebody else. Simple as that," Wembanyama said on 60 Minutes about how his blood clots changed how he looked at life .

While it may seem like that is only affected his personal life, it has certainly affected his game as well. He is much more expressive with his game, and his emotions drive him to perform much better, as seen in the series against the Oklahoma City Thunder in the Western Conference Finals.

As long as Wemby continues to improve his game and regulation his emotions better, he will continue to be a star player. He is ready to take the next step, and that is to the best human and athlete he can be moving forward.

articles.title: Blue Jays Catcher Snubbed Of Historic Award
articles.summary: Thanks to his strong defensive season in what was his first full campaign as a member of the Toronto Blue Jays, catcher Brandon Valenzuela was named a finali...
articles.body:
Thanks to his strong defensive season in what was his first full campaign as a member of the Toronto Blue Jays, catcher Brandon Valenzuela was named a finalist for the American League Gold Glove Award.

However, he'll have to wait for a different season to take home the award, as it was ultimately claimed by Detroit Tigers catcher Dillon Dingler for a second straight campaign.

Toronto Blue Jays Catcher Brandon Valenzuela Was Snubbed For The Gold Glove Award

This season's recipient of the American League Gold Glove award was Detroit Tigers catcher Dillon Dingler, who took home the award for the second straight season.

Unfortunately, this means that Valenzuela will have to wait for a different season to take home the award, which would have been the first of his career.

However, the good news is that Blue Jays fans can take comfort in his emergence as one of the top defensive players in the American League, and if his upward career trajectory continues, it might not be long before he hears his name called for the award in the future.

Valenzuela Is Coming Off His First Full Year With The Blue Jays

Valenzuela began his professional career with the Padres after signing in 2017. He eventually emerged as a standout in the minors, earning Texas League Player of the Month honors in June 2024 with San Antonio.

Toronto acquired him from San Diego at the 2025 trade deadline in the deal that sent Will Wagner to the Padres. Valenzuela spent the rest of the season with Triple-A Buffalo before being protected on the Blue Jays' 40-man roster.

He started 2026 in Buffalo but quickly reached the majors when Toronto needed catching depth following Alejandro Kirk's injury. Valenzuela debuted in early April and recorded his first MLB homer five days later against the Twins .

He would finish the 2026 campaign hitting .226 with nine home runs and 24 RBI, along with a .688 OPS.
